title: Toad in the Hole
subtitle: British pork sausages baked in Yorkshire pudding batter
excerpt: Toad in the hole is a British classic: pork sausages browned in a hot tin and then submerged in Yorkshire pudding batter, which puffs up around the sausages as it bakes. The result is a magnificent puff of golden batter enclosing sausages that are juicy inside and slightly caramelised from the fat. Served with onion gravy, it is one of the great British comfort dishes.
sourceNotes: Toad in the hole appears in British cookbooks from the 18th century. The original recipes used cheaper cuts of meat or leftovers; pork sausages became standard in the 19th century. The name is thought to refer to the way the sausages peek out from the batter like toads from holes in the ground. The dish is a close relative of Yorkshire pudding, using the same batter.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The batter improves with 30 minutes of resting -- make it ahead and refrigerate.

content.text: The same rules as Yorkshire pudding apply: the fat must be smoking hot before the batter goes in, and the oven door must not be opened for at least 20 minutes. The sausages should be browned in the tin first -- this renders their fat, which is what you then use to make the batter rise.
Make the batter: whisk {{plain-flour}} flour, {{eggs}} eggs, {{whole-milk}} milk, and {{salt-table}} salt together until smooth. Rest in the fridge for at least 30 minutes.

Preheat the oven to 220C. Put {{vegetable-oil}} oil in a large roasting tin and heat in the oven for 5 minutes. Add {{pork-sausages}} sausages and turn to coat in oil. Return to the oven for 15 minutes until starting to brown and the fat is sizzling.

Quickly pour the cold batter over and around the sausages. Return to the oven immediately and bake for 25 to 30 minutes without opening the door until the batter is puffed, golden, and crisp at the edges. Serve with onion gravy and roasted vegetables.

items.symptom: The batter is flat and stodgy
items.cause: The fat was not hot enough, or the oven door was opened during baking.
items.fix: The fat must be smoking before the batter goes in. Work fast -- have the batter ready to pour the moment the sausage tin comes out of the oven. Do not open the oven door for the first 20 minutes under any circumstances.

content.text: Toad in the hole is a staple of British school dinners, pub menus, and family suppers. It is one of the most universally known British dishes and appears on menus in British restaurants abroad. The dish is almost always served with onion gravy and mashed potato -- a combination that produces one of the most satisfying meals in the British repertoire.
